curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Letter-Sound Safari!
curatorBrief.intent: Introduce Kindergarten learners to Letter-Sound Group 2 (c, k, e, h, r, m, d) making the sounds /k/, /e/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/, while reviewing Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) in a cumulative 13-letter set.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Letter-Sound Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d. Introduce the new sounds (/k/, /ĕ/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/) while systematically reviewing the sounds from Group 1, pulling from the full 13-letter cumulative list (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d), noting that 'c' and 'k' share the same primary sound /k/.

components.title: Spot the Letters: Group 2 and Review
components.intent: Help kindergarteners recognize and discriminate the printed letterforms for Group 2 (c, k, e, h, r, m, d) alongside review letters from Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) using visual discrimination and case matching.

components.title: Hear the Sound, Find the Letter
components.intent: Introduce and identify phoneme-grapheme correspondences for new sounds /k/, /ĕ/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/ (with 'c' and 'k' both linking to /k/) interspersed with cumulative review of s, a, t, i, p, n.

components.title: Blend Sounds Together
components.intent: Reinforce identification of cumulative letter sounds (Group 1 & 2) by blending sounds sequentially into simple decodable words like cat, hen, rip, mat, and kid.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d.

components.title: Say the Sound Aloud
components.intent: Provide live-judged voice practice where the student independently produces continuous sounds and short vowels (m, r, e, and review sounds s, a, i, n) out loud when shown each letter grapheme.

components.title: Grapheme to Sound Challenge
components.intent: Prompt the student to say the corresponding sound or keyword when shown cumulative letters from the full 13-letter set (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d) with cold presentation without first hearing the tutor model it.

finalAssessment.title: Letter-Sound Safari Roundup
finalAssessment.intent: Check spoken or tap identification and independent production of letter sounds across the entire cumulative 13-letter set (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d).

data.title: Super Sound Adventure
data.description: Get ready to look at the letters and say their sounds out loud!
data.gradeLevel: kindergarten students (ages 5-6) - Use clear language, relatable examples, foundational skills, and engaging visuals. Encourage exploration and basic problem-solving.
data.letters: m, r, s, a, i, n, e, t, p, c, k, h, d

problems.question: Which word starts with the /m/ sound?
problems.rationale: Mouse begins with the /m/ sound made by your lips pressing together. Cat starts with the /k/ sound, and dog starts with the /d/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have students press their lips together to feel the vibration when saying /m/. Emphasize the initial sound by stretching it out: 'm-m-mouse'.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /m/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the /m/ sound from other initial consonant sounds like /k/ and /d/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the letter H sound?
problems.rationale: Hat begins with the /h/ sound made by the letter H. Duck starts with the /d/ sound, and ring starts with the /r/ sound. Listening for the gentle puff of air at the start of 'hat' helps identify the letter H sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have learners place a hand in front of their mouths to feel the warm puff of breath when making the /h/ sound in words like 'hat'.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /h/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the letter sound /h/ from /d/ and /r/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which picture starts with the short e sound?
problems.rationale: Egg begins with the short e sound, which sounds like /ĕ/. Apple starts with /ă/ and iguana starts with /ĭ/. Listening for the opening sound helps us connect words to the letter e.
problems.teachingNote: Have children pretend to crack an egg on the side of a pan while saying /ĕ/ to build a multisensory connection for the short e vowel sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial short vowel sound /ĕ/ in spoken words
Distinguish the short vowel sound /ĕ/ from /ă/ and /ĭ/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: The letter C makes the first sound in ___.
problems.rationale: The word 'cat' begins with the letter C, which makes the /k/ sound. In contrast, 'rat' begins with the /r/ sound and 'hen' begins with the /h/ sound. Listening to the starting sound shows that 'cat' correctly completes the sentence.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce that the letter C makes the /k/ sound at the start of 'cat'. Encourage students to isolate the initial phoneme by stretching the word out loud (e.g., /k/-/a/-/t/).
successCriteria: Identify the initial /k/ sound represented by the letter C in familiar words
Distinguish the starting sound of 'cat' from other Group 2 sounds such as /r/ and /h/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which animal starts with the /d/ sound?
problems.rationale: Duck starts with the /d/ sound from Group 2. Snake begins with /s/ and tiger begins with /t/, which are both sounds from Group 1. Listening closely to the first sound in duck helps us connect it to the letter d.
problems.teachingNote: Have children place their hand lightly on their throat to feel the vocal cord vibration when making the voiced /d/ sound, comparing it with the unvoiced Group 1 sounds like /s/ and /t/.
successCriteria: Identify words that begin with the /d/ sound
Distinguish Group 2 initial sounds from Group 1 initial sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the same sound as cat?
problems.rationale: Kite begins with the /k/ sound, which is the exact same beginning sound heard in cat. Even though cat begins with the letter c and kite begins with the letter k, both letters share this same sound. Sun begins with /s/ and pig begins with /p/.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce that the letter 'c' and the letter 'k' can make the identical /k/ sound. Have students make the sound aloud while touching their throat to feel the shared sound.
successCriteria: Identify words that begin with the /k/ sound represented by letters 'c' and 'k'
Distinguish the /k/ sound from other consonant sounds such as /s/ and /p/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

objectives.notes: The cumulative set requires all 13 letters (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d), but review letters p, n, and i are omitted from letter-sound identification items. Spotter tests letter names rather than sounds.

objectives.objective: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d.
objectives.notes: Every letter in the full 13-letter cumulative set (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d) is directly assessed via unprompted spoken sound production in obj2-di-continuous-production.

detectedConstraints.description: Generator reported unaskableLetters=['i'] in obj2-sound-production-check, preventing the letter 'i' from appearing in keyword match assessment.
obj1-spotter-group2 tests letterform recognition and visual discrimination using letter names rather than phoneme-grapheme correspondences.
Review letters p, n, and i from the cumulative set were not assessed in obj1 identification tasks.

coverage.summary: The lesson thoroughly assesses objective 2 by requiring independent oral production of all 13 letters in the cumulative set via direct instruction review. However, objective 1 is assessed insufficiently because multiple letters from the cumulative set (p, n, and i) are never assessed for sound identification, and the letter-spotter block evaluates letterform recognition by name rather than letter-sound knowledge.
